deep.reconstruction:
This page is a sheet of diagrammatic scratch work on recycled IBM printout. It continues the previous page's argument. The setting is a category (C, W, cof) satisfying Baues' axioms C1–C3, with an initial object. The goal is the classical statement that the inclusion of cofibrant objects induces an equivalence W_cof^{-1}Cof → W^{-1}C.

Two things remain open from the previous page.
(i) Independence of choices: the class [i]^{-1}[φ̃] must not depend on the lift through a weak equivalence i : ỹ ↣~ ỹ'. Diagrams such as x ↣ ȳ ← y with rows of '=' and the pushout ỹ'_1 ∨_ỹ ỹ'_2 compare two choices. They do so through a common refinement and zig-zags of cospans (x →f y ←1 y ; x →h ȳ ←i y ; x →g y ←1 y). The trivial sub-case is also drawn: if i f = h = i g with i ∈ W, then [f] = [g] in the localization.
(ii) The key lemma: x', y' cofibrant, α : y' → y in W, αφ = αψ ⇒ [φ] = [ψ] in W_cof^{-1}Cof. The sketched proof (diagrams 'y∨y → y', 'x∨x → C → y', 'f∨g', 'u', 'x ⇉(k1,k2) C → y') runs as follows.
- Take a cylinder x' ∐ x' ↣ C →~ x' by C3.
- The square formed by (φ,ψ) : x'∐x' → y' and C → x' → y (well defined since αφ = αψ) is fed to the weak lifting lemma. This gives y' ↣~ y'' and a homotopy h : C → y'' with h k1 = iφ and h k2 = iψ.
- Both k1 and k2 are sections of the weak equivalence C → x', so [k1] = [k2] in the localization.
- Hence [iφ] = [iψ], and since i is invertible, [φ] = [ψ].

Other diagrams (x → ỹ' ↣~ ȳ, x∐x ↣ ỹ → ȳ, y →~ ȳ →~ y'', etc.) are variants of these lifting and refinement steps. They are also used for compatibility with composition, which the next page checks: functoriality of [α_x] and inversion of W.

The whole is a standard proof of the 'cofibrant replacement' equivalence in a Brown/Baues cofibration category.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible; the page is fragmentary scratch work. The use of a cylinder for x'∐x' implicitly requires x'∐x' to exist with cofibrant inclusions, i.e. pushouts along cofibrations of cofibrant objects. This is available under Baues' axioms (C1 plus the initial object).

ideas.what: Equivalence W_cof^{-1}Cof ≃ W^{-1}C via a cofibrant replacement functor built with the weak lifting lemma
ideas.modern_name: Cofibrant replacement / Ho(C_cof) ≃ Ho(C) in a cofibration category
ideas.usually_credited_to: K. S. Brown (1973, dual setting), H.-J. Baues (Algebraic Homotopy, 1989; earlier preprints), Quillen for model categories
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in Pursuing Stacks (1983) discussions of 'modelizers'; not as this proof

ideas.what: Maps equalized by a weak equivalence become equal in the localization, proved via a cylinder and the lifting lemma
ideas.modern_name: Left homotopy via cylinder objects; the homotopy relation implies equality in Ho

ideas.what: Independence of choices via the pushout ỹ'_1 ∨_ỹ ỹ'_2 of weak-equivalence cofibrations
ideas.modern_name: Cofinality / calculus of fractions argument in cofibration categories

deep.surprise_reason: These are diagrammatic working notes for a result Grothendieck himself calls 'connu'. It is the standard equivalence Ho(Cof) ≃ Ho(C) in Baues cofibration categories, proved by standard cylinder and lifting arguments. The only historical interest is evidence that Grothendieck was reading Baues' axiomatics around 1982–83.
transcription_corrections: 'x ⇉(k1, g2) C →(gh) y' should read x ⇉(k1, k2) C →(h) y: the two cylinder inclusions followed by the homotopy.
'x ∨ x', 'y ∨ y' denote coproducts (x∐x); 'f ∨ g' is the induced map from the coproduct.
Several 'x' are x̃ or x' (cofibrant replacements), and 'y'' is the target of a weak-equivalence cofibration y' ↣~ y''.
